claim: Feeding of the tobacco hornworm Manduca sexta converts (Z)-3- to (E)-2-GLVs thereby attracting predatory insects.
source_text: Green leaf volatiles (GLVs) constitute a widespread group of defensive plant volatiles that convey a herbivory-specific message via their isomeric composition: feeding of the tobacco hornworm Manduca sexta converts ( Z )-3- to ( E )-2-GLVs thereby attracting predatory insects.

claim: An enzymatic component of M. sexta larval oral secretions adds an herbivory-specific feature to the GLV signal by converting (Z)-3-GLVs to (E)-2-GLVs.
source_text: We recently showed that an enzymatic component of the oral secretions (OS) of M. sexta larvae adds an herbivory-specific feature to the GLV signal. Mechanically damaged leaves of Nicotiana attenuata released large amounts of (Z)-3-GLVs and low amounts of (E)-2-GLVs. However, when the plant was attacked by M. sexta caterpillars or when puncture wounds of plant leaves were treated with M. sexta's OS, the amount of (E)-2-GLVs released increased, while the amount of (Z)-3-GLVs decreased, resulting in a distinct change in the (Z)-3/(E)-2-ratio of GLV emissions.
evidence_reasoning: This references prior work by the authors (Allmann and Baldwin, 2010) and is supported by data in the current manuscript.

evidence_reasoning: This is cited from Rietdorf and Steidle, 2002 and Olsson et al., 2006.

claim: The retention of odor memory learned at the larval stage onto the adult stage has been shown to occur in M. sexta.
source_text: The retention of odor memory learned at the larval stage onto the adult stage has been shown to occur in M. sexta (Blackiston et al., 2008).
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from Blackiston et al., 2008.

claim: The AL has the capacity to resolve the composition of GLV blends as emitted by highly relevant host plants.
source_text: Our results show that the AL, the first odor processing center of the insect brain, has the capacity to resolve the composition of GLV blends as emitted by highly relevant host plants.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the imaging data showing distinct activation patterns for different GLV isomers.

claim: Gravid females prefer oviposition sites with reduced predation and competition risks for their offspring, as indicated by the plant volatile bouquet.
source_text: Correspondingly, gravid females make an informed choice. They prefer oviposition sites with reduced predation and competition risks for their offspring, as indicated by the plant volatile bouquet.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the oviposition preference data and inferred from the ecological context.
